subject: Pre-sales: dedicated GPU sizing — traffic/profile request (GreenBox)
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Emma Torres <emma@greenbox.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pre-sales: dedicated GPU sizing — traffic/profile request (GreenBox)

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the intro call yesterday. To produce a realistic dedicated sizing proposal (ballpark GPUs, autoscale window, and any recommended cache/batching knobs) we need a short workload profile from your side. Can you confirm the items below or attach a short CSV with per-hour counts? If you already have something, the sample file is perfect.

Requested fields (short):
- Peak concurrent sessions (95/99 pctl if you have both)
- Sustained concurrent sessions (typical weekday)
- Average requests per second during steady-state and during peak bursts (RPS)
- Average prompt/token length (tokens or approximate words)
- Average response token length and % of long responses (>1k / >2k tokens)
- Typical model family (Llama2-70B, Llama3-70B, GPT-4x, etc.) and whether you plan to use quantized variants
- Session characteristics: persistent chat (KV cache reuse), stateless prompts, or a mix
- Burst patterns (daily/weekly peaks, marketing spikes, month-end jobs) and their durations
- Any SLAs (p95 latency targets) or priority tiers for traffic
- Batch/async workloads (embeddings, offline rerank) that share the same fleet or a separate job queue

We attached a tiny template (redwood_sizing_template.csv) — a filled hourly sample is ideal. If it's easier, paste a short summary in your reply and we'll draft a preliminary estimate.

Target next steps: once we have the profile, we’ll return a 1-page sizing with assumptions and recommended autoscale bands and then propose a short (30–60m) workshop with infra engineers to validate with synthetic load tests.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: redwood_sizing_template.csv (CSV template — columns: timestamp_hour, rps, concurrent, avg_prompt_tokens, avg_response_tokens, pct_long_responses)

From: Emma Torres <emma@greenbox.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@greenbox.ai
Date: 2027-04-08T12:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pre-sales: dedicated GPU sizing — traffic/profile request (GreenBox)

Hi Vivek —

Thanks — attaching a quick export (greenbox_sample_traffic.csv) and a short summary below. We don’t have hourly data for every metric but this should be close for initial sizing.

Summary (GreenBox prod candidate):
- Typical sustained concurrency: 120 sessions (weekday business hours 08:00–18:00 PT)
- Peak concurrency (burst): 420 sessions (spikes last ~10–20 minutes; marketing-driven)
- Typical steady-state RPS: 35 RPS; peak burst RPS up to 210 RPS
- Avg prompt length: 230 tokens (engineering prompts ~180; user chat ~300)
- Avg response length: 480 tokens; ~18% responses >1000 tokens, ~6% >2000 tokens
- Model: Llama2-70B q4_0 quantized for most traffic; occasional experiments with a Llama3-70B variant
- Chat sessions keep a short KV prefix (avg 28 tokens reused across the session) — we expect cache hit for ~75% of requests in active sessions
- Embeddings: nightly batch job (midnight PT) — separate queue, not latency sensitive
- SLA: p95 < 1.2s for interactive flows; higher for async/embeddings

Notes: we’d like a dedicated pool (isolated from other tenants) with predictable tails for billing/commit. Budget sensitivity around autoscale (prefer short bursts rather than large committed fleets).

Thanks — happy to clarify anything.

—Emma
Emma Torres
CTO, GreenBox AI
emma@greenbox.ai
Attachment: greenbox_sample_traffic.csv (hourly RPS/concurrency sample)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Emma Torres <emma@greenbox.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-08T16:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pre-sales: dedicated GPU sizing — traffic/profile request (GreenBox)

Emma —

Appreciate the detail and the sample — that lets us do a preliminary mapping. High-level assumptions I used for a ballpark:
- Model: Llama2-70B quantized (q4_0) on A100-80/RTX8000-class GPUs; we'll assume runtime optimizations (KV cache, prefix reuse, continuous batching) are enabled.
- Effective throughput per GPU (assumption for sizing): ~20–40 tokens/sec for interactive workloads at low latency — exact depends on prompt+response length and attention/kernel mix.
- Because ~18% of responses are long (>1k tokens) we size for tail tolerance: planning for autoscale headroom to absorb 10–15 minute marketing spikes.

Prelim recommendation (ballpark):
- Committed pool: 8 x A100-80GB equivalents for steady-state (covers sustained 120 concurrent with latency headroom under stated assumptions)
- Autoscale floor/ceiling: autoscale up to 14 GPUs for sustained 10–20 minute spikes (covers 420 concurrent and long-response tail)
- Burst policy: rapid 3–5 minute scale-up with conservative cooldown of 12 minutes to avoid thrash; consider a short warm pool of 2 GPUs for microbursts

What I’ll do next:
- Attach a short workbook (redwood_prelim_estimate_v1.xlsx) with the math and sensitivity rows (tokens/sec per GPU, batching factors, KV cache hit impact).
- Ask engineering to validate token/sec assumptions with a synthetic workload that matches your sample.
- Suggest a 45-minute workshop next week to agree on workload mixes and run a small staging test.

Open questions for engineering check:
- Do you expect concurrent sessions to keep the same session id (full KV reuse) or do they often restart context? That impacts cache hit assumption.
- Any hard entitlement/approval required for short autoscale bursts from procurement?

If this high-level looks sane, I’ll schedule the workshop and loop in our perf team.

Cheers,
Vivek
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood_prelim_estimate_v1.xlsx (workbook — sensitivity table and assumptions)

Key checks:
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU for 480-token avg response + 230-token prompt with KV reuse ~75%
- Latency p95 estimate at steady-state and under 400–450 concurrency burst
- Batching policy: recommend continuous batching with a 5–10ms queuing window for better throughput without large latency increases
